title: Sara Duterte spokesman invokes free speech amid impeachment court's show-cause order
summary: Lawyer Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, on Friday invoked the constitutional right to free speech following the Senate impeachment court's issuance of a show cause order…

blocks.text: Lawyer Paolo Panelo, spokesperson of Vice President Sara Duterte, on Friday invoked the constitutional right to free speech following the Senate impeachment court's issuance of a show cause order against him.
Earlier, Panelo made a comment that some senator-judges were acting as prosecutors.
In a statement, Panelo cited Supreme Court rulings recognizing the right of citizens to scrutinize and criticize public officials, including members of the judiciary.
He quoted the 2012 Supreme Court ruling in Garcia, Jr. v. Manrique, which stated that the power to punish for contempt does not place courts beyond public scrutiny or legitimate criticism.

Panelo also cited the April 8, 2026 ruling in Tolentino v. Heydarian, which emphasized that public discussions on matters of significant public interest should remain free and that courts must be wary of using their contempt powers to suppress critical speech.

"I welcome the opportunity to demonstrate that my comments were fair, made in good faith, and did not impede, obstruct, or degrade the administration of justice, and are thus constitutionally protected," Panelo said.
According to him, he would formally respond to the show cause order within the prescribed period upon receiving it.
The Senate impeachment court on Friday issued the show cause order against Panelo over his comments regarding the alleged partiality of several senator-judges. —NB, GMA News
